ruleName: Ball Lost or Out of Bounds: Stroke-and-Distance Relief Must Be Taken
title: Are White Stakes Themselves Out of Bounds?
question: White stakes define out of bounds. Is the stake itself in bounds?

choices.text: No, the stake itself is out of bounds.
Only if a Local Rule says so.
Only if the committee marks it as such.

explanation: The boundary edge of the course is defined by the course-side points of the white stakes at ground level. The stakes themselves are out of bounds.
imagePrompt: Create a polished, modern semi-realistic illustration (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) in the established junior golf quiz style. Show the edge of a golf course with rough grass transitioning to longer, wild grass behind a clear white out of bounds stake. Place a golf ball on the in-bounds side, close to but not touching the white stake. Include a golfer on the course side looking at the ball and stake. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer observes a golf ball lying just in bounds next to a white out of bounds stake at the edge of a golf course.
